text:
Summary
 Phones will carry most of this holiday's online spend, and buy now pay later is growing on mobile too. This guide gives seven fixes a WooCommerce store can make this week, from a shorter checkout and wallet buttons to BNPL placement, lighter forms, guest checkout, speed and real-device testing, so your checkout holds up before Black Friday.


 
 Introduction
 Most stores spend the weeks before Black Friday on promotions and ads. Far fewer check whether a shopper on a phone can actually finish paying. That is where sales slip away fastest, because there is nothing left to persuade. The shopper has already decided to buy.
 This article stays on checkout and payments for mobile. If you want the promotion and traffic side, start with our Black Friday website preparation guide .

 Frequently Asked Questions 

 
 Why does mobile checkout decide your holiday sales?
 Shoppers have not stopped using phones, and the holiday numbers make that plain. Adobe's 2026 forecast puts mobile at 57.4% of online holiday spend, up from 56.4% last year, and at a record 63% in its Thanksgiving outlook. Buy now pay later (BNPL) is forecast at $21.3 billion for November and December, and 82% of that spend comes through mobile.
 That means your busiest days will be decided on a 6-inch screen, usually with one hand, often while the shopper is doing something else. A checkout that feels fine on your office monitor can lose people at every tap. Cyber Monday falls on November 30, and Black Friday is November 27, so the window to fix things is short.
 The seven fixes below are small enough to finish this week. They are specific to WooCommerce, and they stay on checkout and payments. For the wider set of store problems, see our guide to ecommerce UX problems that drive customers away .


 Fix 1: Is your checkout built for one thumb?
 Count the taps between "Add to cart" and "Place order" on your own phone. Every extra page, scroll and pop-up is a chance to leave. The aim is a single, clear path: cart, then checkout, then done.
 Newer versions of WooCommerce use the Checkout block by default on new stores, and it puts contact, shipping, payment and order summary on one page. If your store still uses the older shortcode checkout, test the block version on a staging copy. Check that your shipping, tax and payment extensions work with it before you switch, because a few older plugins do not.
 Keep the order summary collapsed by default on mobile, with the total always visible. Make the Place order button large, full width and easy to reach with a thumb.



 Fix 2: Are wallet buttons at the top of the page?
 Wallet buttons such as Apple Pay, Google Pay and PayPal let a shopper pay without typing a card number or an address. On a phone, that is the difference between ten seconds and two minutes.
 WooCommerce payment extensions from Stripe, PayPal and WooPayments offer these buttons. Turn them on for the cart page, the product page and the top of checkout, not only the bottom. Then check the details: the button should show the right shipping options and the final total, and it should work for guest shoppers.
 Test each wallet on the device it belongs to. Apple Pay needs Safari on an iPhone, and Google Pay needs Chrome on Android. A button that appears but fails at the last step costs more than no button at all.
 One more setup step matters here. Set your shipping and tax rules before you enable wallets, because express checkout skips the normal form and relies on your saved rules to calculate the total. If a wallet shows the wrong shipping price or tax, shoppers see it at the very last moment and many will stop.




 Fix 3: Where should buy now pay later appear?
 BNPL works best when shoppers see it early, before they decide the price is too high. Add the "pay in four" message to the product page and the cart, near the price, and keep the full option in checkout. Providers such as Klarna, Afterpay and Affirm each offer WooCommerce extensions, so compare fees, approval flow and terms before you choose.
 Keep the message short and honest. Show the real instalment amount, and avoid language that hides what the shopper is agreeing to. BNPL tends to suit mid-priced and higher-priced baskets, so you may want to set a minimum order value to show it.
 One more point on mobile: the provider's pop-up or redirect must open cleanly on a phone and return the shopper to your order confirmation page. Place a sandbox order and watch what happens at each step.
 Also think about refunds. When a BNPL order is refunded, the money usually goes back through the provider, so make sure your team knows how to process it from the WooCommerce order screen and what to tell the customer. Holiday returns arrive in January, and your support team should not be learning this on the first refund.




 Fix 4: Are you asking for fields shoppers do not need?
 Every field you ask for is a small tax on the shopper's patience, and typing on glass is slow. Review your checkout form and remove what you do not need to ship the order.
 In the Checkout block settings you can make the company name and phone number optional or hide them. Address line 2 can usually be collapsed behind a link. If you do collect a phone number, explain why, for example "for delivery updates".
 Then fix the small things. Email, phone and postcode fields should open the right keyboard. Turn on browser autofill and address lookup if your host or plugin supports it. Inline error messages should say exactly what to fix, in plain words, next to the field.


 Fix 5: Can a shopper check out without making an account?
 Forcing an account before payment is one of the oldest ways to lose a sale. In WooCommerce, go to WooCommerce, then Settings, then Accounts and Privacy, and turn on guest checkout. You can still offer account creation after the order, with a single checkbox or a button on the thank-you page.
 If you want repeat buyers, give them a reason to sign in later, such as order tracking or a faster reorder. Do not make them pay for that choice at the moment they are ready to buy.


 Fix 6: Is the checkout page fast on a mid-range phone?
 Slow checkout pages leak orders, and phones on mobile data make it worse. Google's guidance for good Core Web Vitals is a Largest Contentful Paint under 2.5 seconds and an Interaction to Next Paint under 200 milliseconds. Checkout is the page where the second number matters most, because every tap should feel instant.
 Start with what you can remove. Chat widgets, pop-ups, heat-map scripts and extra tracking tags often load on checkout when they do not need to. Exclude the cart, checkout and account pages from page caching, because cached checkout pages cause stale totals and login problems. Compress images, load fonts sparingly, and test on a mid-range Android phone, not only the latest iPhone.
 If you want a baseline, run the checkout URL through PageSpeed Insights on mobile and fix the top two items before Black Friday.


 Fix 7: Have you placed a test order on a real phone?
 The cheapest fix on this list is also the one most stores skip. Before the sale, place real test orders on real phones: an iPhone on Safari, an Android on Chrome, and one on a slow connection.
 Run through each payment route: card, each wallet, and BNPL in sandbox mode. Try a coupon, a shipping change and a failed card. Check that the confirmation page loads and that the order email arrives. Write down every place you hesitated, because your customers will hesitate there too.
 Do this again after every plugin or theme update. Your peak days are not the time to find out an update broke the Place order button. Our Black Friday preparation guide covers the promotion and traffic side of the same weekend.



 Which fix should you do first?
 If you only have a day, start with fixes that remove the most friction for the least work. Turn on guest checkout and trim the form fields first, since both are settings changes. Add wallet buttons next. Place BNPL messaging after that, then work on speed. Finish with the full device test, and repeat it once more the week before Black Friday.
 If your analytics show most of your drop-off happens on the payment step, move wallets and BNPL to the front. If drop-off happens earlier, on the cart or shipping step, begin with the checkout layout.


 What mistakes hurt mobile checkout most during a sale?
 Even stores that do the seven fixes above can lose orders to a handful of repeat mistakes. These are the ones we see most often in the weeks around Black Friday.
 The first is adding things at the last minute. Stores often install a new pop-up, upsell plugin or loyalty widget the week of the sale. Each one adds scripts to checkout, and each one can clash with payment buttons. Freeze plugin changes on checkout at least a week before Black Friday.
 The second is shipping surprises. Shoppers on a phone leave quickly when the shipping cost appears only at the last step. Show a shipping estimate or a free shipping threshold in the cart, and make sure the delivery dates you promise for holiday orders are realistic.
 The third is coupon trouble. A coupon box that is easy to tap sends shoppers off to search for codes, and many do not come back. Apply sale discounts automatically where you can, keep the coupon field behind a link, and test that stacked offers calculate the way you expect.
 The fourth is ignoring payment failures. Declined cards, 3-D Secure windows that never return and wallet errors all look like lost sales with no message attached. After the first sale day, review your payment gateway logs and the WooCommerce order notes for failed attempts, and fix any pattern quickly.


 What should your pre-Black Friday checkout checklist include?
 Use this simple timeline so the work does not pile up in the last few days.
 Two weeks out: finish the checkout layout, guest checkout and form fields, and install your wallet and BNPL extensions. Place your first round of test orders and fix what breaks.
 One week out: run the speed test again, remove scripts you do not need, and freeze plugin and theme updates. Ask your host about caching rules and resource limits, and confirm the plan can handle peak traffic.
 Sale week: repeat the full device test, check that order and payment emails arrive, and make sure your support team can answer questions about wallet payments and BNPL.
 During the sale: watch orders, failed payments and error logs every day, and keep a developer on call. A small problem found at 9 a.m. costs far less than the same problem found at 9 p.m.

 Conclusion
 Mobile checkout is where holiday revenue is won or lost, and most of the fixes are settings, small plugin changes and a bit of testing. Shorten the path, put wallets first, show BNPL early, cut the fields, allow guests, keep the page light and test on real phones.
 Start this week, finish at least a week before Black Friday, and leave the days right before the sale for watching, not changing.
 

 Frequently Asked Questions
 How much of holiday online shopping happens on mobile? 
 According to Adobe's 2026 holiday forecast, mobile will account for 57.4% of online spend over the full season and a record 63% in its Thanksgiving outlook. Your own analytics matter more than any forecast, so check your mobile share before you decide how much to invest.
 
 

 Does buy now pay later increase sales on a WooCommerce store? 
 It can help on mid-priced and higher-priced baskets, but results vary by store and provider. Test it on a few products, compare conversion and average order value, and read the provider's fees and terms before you roll it out across the whole catalog.
 
 

 Should I use the WooCommerce Checkout block or the classic checkout? 
 The Checkout block is the default on newer stores and handles wallet buttons and mobile layout well. Test it on a staging copy first, because some older plugins do not support it yet.
 
 

 Do I need guest checkout turned on? 
 For most stores, yes. Requiring an account adds a step at the worst possible moment. Offer account creation after the order instead.
 
 

 How early should I finish checkout changes before Black Friday? 
 Aim to finish at least a week ahead, so you have time to test on real devices and fix problems. Avoid big changes in the days right before the sale.
